item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Storytelling -- works by Adira Rotstein — Sun Nov 1, 12:00 AM — Deer Park
item.description: Throughout the month of November, the works of artist Adira Rotstein are on display at Deer Park branch . Adira Rotstein is a Toronto artist, writer and teacher. Her YA novels 'Little Jane Silver' and 'Little Jane and the Nameless Isle' are published by Dundurn. She has experience in sequential art, creating comic books and illustrating stories. She also loves experimenting with the boundaries of stopmotion and hand drawn animation. I am curious about the world in all beauty and absurdity "Usually, with my artwork I attempt to tell a story. People say I am able to imbue even inanimate objects with a personality, human agency and warmth. People's faces, their motions, their discarded objects at rest tell stories about where they have been, what they have felt and where they are going. Slow down and see what they have to say. item.title: Silvia Bonoli (Donostia International Physics Center) — Mon Nov 2, 3:00 PM — MP 1318A
item.description:
Title: Constraining the growth of massive black holes with a population-level multi-messenger approach
Abstract: JWST’s discovery of a large population of active black holes at z > 5, and the evidence from Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs) for a gravitational-wave background likely produced by supermassive black hole binaries, offer new constraints on the growth and evolution of massive black holes. Both observations challenge standard expectations. JWST points to more numerous or more rapidly growing black holes at earlier times than many models predict, while the estimated PTA amplitude seems to require a larger-than-expected population of very massive black holes at low redshift. Meanwhile, tidal disruption events (TDEs) open a window onto the elusive population of intermediate-mass black holes. item.title: Continental Philosophy Research Group (Thimo Heisenberg, Rice University) — Thu Nov 5, 3:00 PM — Jackman Humanities Building
item.description: The Continental Philosophy Research Interest Group welcomes guest speaker Thimo Heisenberg, an associate professor in the Department of Philosophy at Rice University. Professor Heisenberg is a specialist in 19th and 20th century German Philosophy. Having earned his PhD from Columbia in 2019, his work has appeared in journals such as the British Journal of the History of Philosophy, the European Journal of Philosophy, Inquiry, and the Journal of the American Philosophical Association, as well as in many edited collections and anthologies. He was a Fulbright Scholar, and has received fellowships from the Alexander-von-Humboldt Foundation, the German National Academic Foundation, the Max Weber Program and from Columbia University. His book, The Economy in German Idealism, is under contract with Oxford University Press. item.title: Copilot como tu primer asistente de IA: diseña un asistente para una tarea real — Fri Nov 6, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto ¿Qué pasaría si no tuvieras que explicarle a Copilot desde cero lo que necesitas cada vez que trabajas con él?
En esta sesión práctica aprenderemos a diseñar un asistente de IA especializado utilizando Microsoft Copilot. Partiremos de una necesidad concreta y construiremos paso a paso su propósito, contexto, instrucciones, tareas, límites y resultados esperados.
Trabajaremos con una estructura sencilla: Propósito → Rol → Contexto → Instrucciones → Tareas → Límites → Resultado esperado El objetivo no será construir un agente autónomo complejo, sino comprender y experimentar con los elementos fundamentales que necesitamos para convertir Copilot en un asistente diseñado para un propósito específico.
Source: Meetup: Microsoft Reactor Toronto

item.title: Surviving Dementia Care: The Realities of Family Caregiving With D. Grant Campbell — Fri Nov 6, 2:00 PM — St. Clair/Silverthorn
item.description:
This program will address the experiences of families who are caring for a loved one who is living with dementia, including the various points of stress, as well as the various points of joy, and ways in which caregivers learn to survive the experience. Major topics include understanding the diagnosis, communicating with the loved one, choosing an assisted living facility, and using music and the arts as a means of connection.
Source: Toronto Public Library — Older Adults

item.description:

A book talk on Against Tech Oligarchy, an account of the rise of the tech worker movement and the industry backlash it provoked. The book traces how tech workers organized against their employers over military contracts, sexism and working conditions, and how Silicon Valley’s labour politics shifted in response.
